summary: This lecture is part 67 of Sheikh Ali Mashhour's detailed commentary on Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter), Ibn al-Qayyim's comprehensive work on the life and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad. The lecture begins with discussion of Ibn al-Qayyim's remarkable feat of writing the entire book from memory while traveling to Hajj, citing over 300 sources verbatim. The sheikh explains the intentional non-sequential organization of the book, comparing it to how classical scholars like Ibn Hibban deliberately scattered their works to encourage thorough study and retention. The bulk of this session focuses on introducing the topic of fasting (sawm), providing its linguistic and legal definitions, explaining the two pillars of fasting (intention and abstention from dawn to sunset), and clarifying common misconceptions about when fasting begins and ends.
